title: Every Oklahoma Sooner Picked No. 1 Overall in the NFL Draft
question: How many Oklahoma Sooners have been the No. 1 overall pick in the NFL Draft?
answer: Five Sooners have gone first overall: Lee Roy Selmon (1976), Billy Sims (1980), Sam Bradford (2010), Baker Mayfield (2018) and Kyler Murray (2019). That ties Oklahoma with Georgia and Notre Dame for second-most, one behind USC.
summary: Five Sooners have gone No. 1 overall in the NFL Draft, from Lee Roy Selmon in 1976 to Kyler Murray in 2019. See the full list with teams and OU years.
body: Few programs have sent players to the very top of the NFL Draft as often as Oklahoma. Five times a former Sooner has been the first name called, and by ESPN's 2026 tally of schools with the most No. 1 overall picks, only USC, with six, has more. Georgia and Notre Dame share the five-pick tier with OU.

The list opens with Lee Roy Selmon (OU 1972-75), the 1975 consensus All-American who swept the Outland and Lombardi trophies. The expansion Tampa Bay Buccaneers made him the first draft choice in franchise history in 1976. Four years later, 1978 Heisman winner Billy Sims (OU 1975-79) went first to the Detroit Lions.

Then came a three-decade wait. Oklahoma City native Sam Bradford (OU 2006-09, redshirting in 2006) went No. 1 to the St. Louis Rams in 2010 and was named AP Offensive Rookie of the Year after passing for 3,512 yards that fall. He was the third Sooner taken first overall.

The most remarkable stretch arrived at the end of the 2010s. Baker Mayfield (OU 2014-17, after one season at Texas Tech) went first to the Cleveland Browns in 2018. One year later, Kyler Murray (OU 2016-18, after a freshman year at Texas A&M) went first to the Arizona Cardinals, giving Oklahoma quarterbacks the top pick in back-to-back drafts. Each had won the Heisman Trophy the December before his draft.

Quick recap for your next tailgate: one defensive lineman, one running back and three quarterbacks, spread across four different decades. When the trivia question is which schools keep landing the NFL Draft's top slot, Oklahoma belongs in the first breath of the answer.
